prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was reversing out of a space when it contacted the claimant's parked vehicle. Claimant reports being struck on the head by the airbag deployment and has been diagnosed with a concussion. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Photos of both vehicles requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes persistent headache, light sensitivity, and dizziness since the incident. Advised claimant of the medical payments coverage available under the policy and provided the forms needed to submit treatment records. Claimant stated they understand they may contact their own attorney at any time.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles. Damage to claimant's rear bumper and tail light is consistent with the reported impact. Insured's front bumper shows scuffing. Scene diagram obtained from insured. No independent witnesses identified so far. Parking lot security footage requested from property owner.

Entry 4: Claimant submitted medical report confirming a concussion diagnosis and recommended a period of rest and follow-up with a neurologist. Reviewed report with claimant, who asked for an explanation of the next steps. Explained the claim review process in plain terms and confirmed the adjuster's direct line for questions. Vehicle inspection scheduled with the appraiser.

Entry 5: Security footage received from the lot operator. Footage shows the insured's vehicle reversing at low speed and contacting the claimant's vehicle. Liability for the collision appears clear. Bodily injury evaluation remains open pending the neurologist's follow-up report. Claimant informed of status and reminded of the right to seek independent legal advice before accepting any settlement.
